notes: India domestic backbone, 175 driver->driver edges. Design: (1) F_GDP_IN is an output aggregate fed by expenditure components (govt/private capex, urban/rural consumption, housing, monsoon agri output, INR net exports); income feedback runs GDP->wages/credit->consumption so there is no direct GDP->consumption edge (avoids double counting). (2) Monetary transmission split into price-of-credit edges (repo->housing/auto/urban/capex/credit) plus a small direct repo->CPI expectations edge; undamped summed paths give ~-0.5 pp CPI and ~-0.85 pp GDP per 100 bp (~-0.35/-0.6 after order damping), inside the RBI QPM 2.0 range. (3) Policy reaction functions: CPI/GDP/INR->repo, CPI/GDP->liquidity, INR->FX reserves->liquidity (reuses india_macro's NEW_FX_RESERVES_IN), food inflation->agri trade curbs and sugar policy, Brent and fiscal slippage->fuel excise, fertiliser inputs->subsidy, INR->gold duty (May-2026 6->15%), India-Pakistan->defence procurement, credit boom/GDP->RBI prudential, equity activity->SEBI derivatives/STT. All 2-node cycles have |w product| <= 0.24. Discretionary fiscal stimulus (GST cuts, tax relief, transfers) is NOT given a GDP reaction edge - model as events. Undamped path-sum checks (<=4 steps): repo +25 bp -> CPI -0.13 pp, GDP -0.21 pp; INR +3% -> CPI +0.27 pp, liquidity -Rs1.5 lakh cr; monsoon +10% -> CPI -0.23 pp, GDP +0.64 pp; GST broad cut -> auto volumes +16%. (4) Left to the global backbone: Brent/gas/coal/gold/DXY/US-yield/VIX/China->Indian prices, rupee, FPI and power cost edges (only the policy reaction F_BRENT->P_FUEL_TAX_IN and F_FERTILISER_INPUTS->P_FERT_SUBSIDY are included here), coal->power price, steel duty and China steel. Two Indian-policy->world-price edges included (agri curbs->rice, sugar policy->sugar). Calibration anchors: RBI MPR Oct-2026 scenario elasticities (INR 5% -> CPI +40 bp, GDP +25 bp; rain-shortfall agri coefficient -0.40; bank-lending-channel IRF; transmission table), 2024-base CPI food+beverage weight 36.5%, GST 2.0 (-85 bp CPI; PV sales +16-20 pp), WGC gold-duty response (-10% demand for +9 pp), SEBI FY26 F&O study (-18% traders), Mar-2026 Rs10/l excise cut. Caveats: monsoon edges are asymmetric (use mainly for deficits; 2026 monsoon -12.6% of LPA = -1.26 SSU); policy reactions are lumpy and state-dependent (supply vs demand shocks) - treat as expected values; theme SSUs (+1) are undefined notches, interpreted here as a clearly visible acceleration; P_FERT_SUBSIDY +1 interpreted as ~Rs30k cr more support.
